title: Salary Sacrifice Flights and Your Annual Pay: A Guide for Australian Workers
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, and how salary sacrifice flights can affect your take-home pay.
salarySummary: For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,265 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

faqs.q: Does salary sacrifice for flights affect my super?
faqs.a: Yes, salary sacrifice flights reduce your ordinary time earnings, which is the base for calculating your super guarantee. Your employer must pay super on your reduced salary, but only up to the maximum contribution base. Salary sacrifice can lower your taxable income but may also reduce your super contributions if not structured carefully.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement, set by the Fair Work Commission. Award rates are higher minimums for specific industries or occupations, set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Many workers are entitled to award rates, which include penalties and allowances. The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for 38 hours.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia

If you earn an hourly wage or receive a salary offer, understanding your annual pay is essential for budgeting, tax planning, and comparing job opportunities. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For full-time employees, the typical assumption is 38 hours per week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. If you work part-time or casual hours, simply replace 38 with your actual weekly hours.

### Example Using the National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour. For a 38-hour week:

- Weekly pay: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90
- Fortnightly pay: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80
- Annual gross pay: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,265.44

This is the minimum before tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation. Note that many employees are covered by award rates, which are higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, the General Retail Industry Award may set a higher minimum for retail workers. Always check your specific award or agreement via [pay guides](/blog).

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using [the timesheet](/), you can enter your base hourly rate and check a box to add casual loading. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it automatically.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary time earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% (from 1 July 2026), applied to your gross pay up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For the minimum wage example, super would be $52,265.44 × 12% = $6,271.85, paid by your employer on top of your salary.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). For the minimum wage earner ($52,265), the tax would be approximately $5,092 plus $1,045 Medicare levy, leaving a take-home pay of around $46,128. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a detailed breakdown.

### Salary Sacrifice Flights and Your Annual Pay

Salary sacrifice flights are a common benefit offered by some employers, allowing you to use pre-tax income to pay for flights. This reduces your taxable income, which can lower your tax bill. However, it also reduces your ordinary time earnings for super guarantee purposes. For example, if you salary sacrifice $5,000 for flights, your gross pay for super calculation drops to $47,265, and your super contribution would be $5,671.80 instead of $6,271.85. The trade-off is lower tax now but potentially less super later.

When converting your hourly rate to annual pay, remember that salary sacrifice arrangements are not included in the simple formula. Our calculator assumes no salary sacrifice, so you should adjust your annual figure manually if you have such an arrangement. For more on how packaging affects your pay, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Not all workers earn the same. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That equates to an annual salary of about $108,352 – well above the minimum wage. However, this is an average across all industries and states, not a median for your specific job. If you are comparing job offers, use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) reference tables to see industry and state averages.

For casual workers, the average total earnings (including part-time) is $1,579.20 per week, or $82,118 annually. Again, these are averages, not your personal median. Always check your award or agreement for your exact rate.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and instantly see annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Select the casual loading checkbox if applicable. The calculator uses the standard 38-hour week but you can adjust hours. Remember: the results are estimates. They do not include unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, stopping at the maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident rates with the full tax-free threshold.

### Key Takeaways

- Annual pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52
- Assume 38 hours for full-time; adjust for part-time or casual
- Casual loading is 25% on top of base rate
- Super is 12% paid on top of ordinary earnings
- Salary sacrifice flights reduce taxable income and super base
- Use the timesheet for quick conversions, but consult a professional for binding advice

For more detailed information, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman for award rates and the Australian Taxation Office for tax and super rules.
